title: Client-Server
subtitle: Clients ask, servers answer, and the state has to live somewhere
motto: Make servers forgettable, so any one of them can fail
coreAddition: stateless servers behind a load balancer
keyInsight: Spreading load across servers is easy; deciding where each user's session lives is what decides whether a crash costs you users.

decisions.title: Show sessions, not just load
decisions.description: The failure frame reports the share of users who lose their session, because a stateful crash is a user-visible event, not only a capacity event.
decisions.alternatives: Modeling only utilization would show the servers coping and hide the lost logins, which is the real cost of stateful servers.

decisions.title: Compare after a crash with one fewer server
decisions.description: Both the stateful and stateless frames are measured with a server gone, so the capacity headroom (N+1) is part of the lesson.
decisions.alternatives: Measuring only the healthy fleet makes both designs look equally fine and skips the reason to over-provision.
